# FlinkEval: A Synthetic Corpus for Evaluating Natural Language Interfaces to Streaming SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#flinkeval)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-14**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.17093v1) · arXiv:2611.17093v1, 12 November 2026; experiments distinguish corpus releases v3.1 and v2

**Reading coverage:** All 17 PDF pages: Sections 1–6, limitations, references, Appendices A–E, all 13 tables, corpus-generation and validation protocols, model/judge configuration, paired statistical comparisons and illustrative SQL/dialogue examples. Tables 3–4 and their qualifications were visually inspected on PDF page 6. The PDF was used because the HTML conversion omits later appendix text and references.

## Research question

Streaming SQL adds temporal and operational constraints, while underspecified requests complicate judging whether a query disagrees with one reference or with the user's intended meaning.

## Method

Builds synthetic schemas, data and SQL through validation and repair, then creates seven request conditions spanning explicit wording, attempted semantics-preserving reformulation, and business-language requests with zero to three ranked oracle clues. Three model judges adjudicate reference-anchored and face-value criteria.

## Evaluation

Describes 3,903 pairs across 45 domains. Five models are compared on 666 selected test questions; the ladder uses one model on 600 questions with verified variants. Known window failures exclude 115 test items. Execution-error rates are reported separately from judge-pass rates; no streaming execution-equivalence accuracy is computed.

## What the results support

Oracle clues raise reference-anchored judge-pass from 27.0% to 51.3%, while face-value rates remain approximately 73–75%. All 81 background predictions in the model comparison fail observed execution despite substantial judged acceptance for several models.

## Limits and qualifications

LLM-generated wording and omissions are confounded, individual ambiguity is unvalidated, and clues are not interactive clarification. Generator/verifier and evaluator families overlap; judgments lack human calibration. Single runs and one cloud deployment limit transfer. Background reference validation does not uniformly execute the complete DML statement.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a streaming setting for studying specification and evaluation-criterion sensitivity, without establishing deployed clarification or abstention performance.
